title: Тайна паспорта  (The Secret of the Passport)

segments.t: During the celebration in the kitchen, Chef Viktor examines Max's passport on the counter. Looking at the official stamp, Viktor notices that Max's birthday is actually in February, uncovering Max's well-intentioned lie. Let's listen to their conversation in Russian first.
А почему день рождения в феврале?
Now let's examine this surprising revelation line by line.
'Show me your passport, Max.' Chef Barinov leads with the direct command form meaning 'show', followed by 'passport'.
'Here is my passport, chef.' Max delivers a punchy conversational reaction built around the Russian word meaning 'passport'.
А почему день рождения в феврале?
'And why is the birthday in February?' Russian omits the present-tense verb 'to be' here, linking 'why' directly with 'day', pairing it with 'of birth' and 'February'.
'Your birthday is not today?' Senya turns a statement into a question purely through rising intonation on the word meaning 'day', pairing it with 'of birth' and 'today'.
'I wanted to please you.' Max chooses the imperfective verb meaning 'wanted' for the ongoing action, followed by 'to do' and 'something pleasant'.
'Did you lie to us about the holiday?' Chef Barinov turns a statement into a question purely through rising intonation on the word meaning 'lied', followed by 'holiday'.
'I wanted to forget all grudges.' Max chooses the imperfective verb meaning 'wanted' for the ongoing action, followed by 'forget' and 'offense'.
'But one must not lie to friends.' Senya chooses the imperfective verb meaning 'to lie' for the ongoing action, followed by 'to friends' and 'not allowed'.
'Any lie is bad.' Russian omits the present-tense verb 'to be' here, linking 'lie' directly with 'badly' to make the point directly in conversation.
'I am very guilty before you.' Russian omits the present-tense verb 'to be' here, linking 'very much' directly with 'at fault', combining 'very much' with 'at fault'.
'For any deceit one must answer.' The phrasing opens with 'any' before bringing in 'a trick' and 'it is necessary' to make the point clear.
'The truth always reveals itself.' Senya expresses this naturally by combining the word for 'honestly' with 'always' and 'is opening'.

'For any deceit one has to pay.' Max puts the word for 'any' together with 'a trick' and 'to have to' in a crisp, natural spoken turn of phrase. Now let's listen to the whole conversation again from start to finish.

Faced with the undeniable proof in his passport, Max realizes that even a lie told for good reasons carries serious consequences. Next time you watch the episode, listen for the Russian expressions for 'to show' and 'passport' — you will catch every word right away. See you in the next scene.
